title: Comparison with Buddy Johnson
summary: Buddy Johnson's band was bluesier and his more swinging.

story.theme_name: Playing with Count Basie: joining, leading, leaving
story.community_name: Playing with Count Basie: the band, its feel and its people

blocks.x: How would you compare your band to a band such as Buddy Johnson's?

Well, you know, I was up here before Buddy. Buddy seemed to have something like on the same type of beat that I had, you know, although he was a little more bluesy than I was. You know? But, I think my band was a little more swingier and a little further up than Buddy. Buddy had a good band. Like, he had Arthur Prysock. Arthur, he's the singer? Wasn't he?
Red. Right. But, Buddy had a good band that drew a lot of people.
They had, he had that same kind of popularity with the masses, you know, that your band had. But, as you said, with less of a jazz emphasis and more of a rhythm and blues.
That kind of a flavor. But, he had that same kind of, oh, I guess, cohesiveness, you know, with the masses in addition.
Right. He certainly did. And, he had his following, too. He drew big, especially with his sister and Arthur in there together. And, he had a good feeling, a good rhythm feeling. Yeah.
